guide.summary: Public app for many YNAB users (app review, wait 2-4 weeks); Prototype or small pilot (up to 25 users) (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Prototype or small pilot (up to 25 users) (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none). Hardest: Public app for many YNAB users (app review, wait 2-4 weeks).

composio.note: Composio manages OAuth for YNAB, so prototypes need no own app. For launch, create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio's managed app works. For a launch under your own brand, with a dedicated quota, or with custom scopes, you need your own YNAB OAuth app, and it needs review to serve more than 25 outside users.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand instead of Composio's

Managed default scopes may not cover what you need

prerequisites.title: YNAB account with Developer Settings
prerequisites.detail: Create the OAuth app under Account Settings, then Developer Settings, then New Application.

prerequisites.title: Public privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Must be displayed to users, show a Last Updated date, and give a way to request data deletion, which can be a contact email. YNAB does not check its legal compliance.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app in YNAB
steps.detail: Sign in, open Developer Settings, click New Application, fill in details and save. Copy the Client ID and Secret.
steps.done_when: You have a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret. Use the redirect URI shown in the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Draft privacy policy and app naming
steps.detail: Draft a policy with Last Updated date and deletion contact. Check the app name and footer against YNAB's branding rules.
steps.done_when: Policy is published and name follows the rules.

steps.title: Request review via YNAB form
steps.detail: Submit the review request form for your app and confirm the privacy policy URL is shown in the OAuth client configuration.

steps.title: Wait for YNAB review
steps.detail: YNAB reviews the app and emails you once Restricted Mode is removed.

traps.title: For the Implicit Grant flow, access tokens expire 2
traps.detail: For the Implicit Grant flow, access tokens expire 2 hours after being granted and cannot be refreshed, so the user must re-authorize (page does not tie this to Restricted Mode).

traps.title: Hard stop at 25 outside users
traps.detail: After 25 tokens, the authorization screen shows a message and new authorizations are blocked. Request review before onboarding past that number.

traps.title: Implicit grant tokens cannot refresh
traps.detail: Access tokens last 2 hours; implicit grant users must re-authorize, while the Authorization Code flow supports refresh tokens.

traps.title: Review wait is 2-4 weeks
traps.detail: Plan the launch date around this wait.

traps.title: Naming rules for your app
traps.detail: The app and its domain cannot contain YNAB or You Need A Budget unless preceded by 'for'. Do not imply YNAB endorses it.

traps.title: Never handle financial account credentials
traps.detail: You may not request, handle or store credentials for users' financial accounts directly.

traps.title: Rate limit of 200 requests per hour
traps.detail: Each access token gets up to 200 requests per hour in a rolling window. YNAB may change limits at its discretion.

traps.title: Read-only tokens cannot write
traps.detail: A token with the read-only scope gets 403 Forbidden on endpoints that modify the plan. Request minimal permissions.

blockers.symptom: Authorization screen shows a limit message and new users cannot authorize
blockers.what_it_means: The app is in Restricted Mode and has hit the 25-token cap.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit the review request form and wait 2-4 weeks.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the privacy policy and check the app against the OAuth Application Requirements before submitting.

open_questions: Does YNAB have a partner program or other approval needed for commercial products? No page was found; ask YNAB API support.
What exactly does Restricted Mode block beyond the 25-token cap? Docs do not say; test or ask YNAB support.

evidence.answer: An access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour, enforced in a rolling window.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: YNAB sets and enforces limits on your use of the APIs at our discretion.
evidence.answer: YNAB sets and enforces API usage limits at its discretion, and those limits may change.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: This process takes 2-4 weeks.
evidence.answer: The page says removing Restricted Mode after a review takes 2-4 weeks.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The YNAB API may only be used when permission is explicitly given by a YNAB account owner through the Authentication processes described in the documentation above.
evidence.answer: API use requires explicit permission from a YNAB account owner given through the documented authentication processes.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The user will be given the option to approve your request for access:
evidence.answer: During authorization, the end user is given the option to approve the app's access request.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When default plan selection is enabled, a user will be asked to select a default plan when authorizing your application:
evidence.answer: If default plan selection is enabled, the user is asked to select a default plan when authorizing the app.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: replacing [CLIENT_ID] and [REDIRECT_URI] with the values configured when creating the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The authorization URL uses the client ID and redirect URI values configured when the OAuth app was created.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: redirect_uri - The same [REDIRECT_URI] sent with the original authorization code request in Step 1 above and specified when setting up the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The redirect URI in the token request must match the one sent in the authorization request and specified in the app setup.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: TLS (a.k.a. SSL or HTTPS) is enforced on all requests to ensure communication from your client to our endpoint is encrypted
evidence.answer: TLS (HTTPS) is enforced on all API requests (the page does not state a separate HTTPS rule for redirect URIs).

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: After saving, you will see the details of the new application, including the Client ID and the Client Secret which are referenced in the instructions below.
evidence.answer: After saving the new OAuth application, its details, including Client ID and Client Secret, are shown.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Here, you specify the details of your application and save it.
evidence.answer: The developer specifies the app's details in the form and saves it.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The YNAB API supports two OAuth grant types: Implicit Grant and Authorization Code Grant
evidence.answer: The YNAB API supports two OAuth grant types: Implicit Grant and Authorization Code Grant.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: client_secret - The client secret provided when setting up the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The Authorization Code flow's token request requires the client secret provided during app setup.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Display the privacy policy URL in your OAuth client configuration when your application is publicly available and ensure that it is prominently displayed in your application interface so that users can find this information easily.
evidence.answer: A privacy policy URL must be shown in the OAuth client configuration once the app is publicly available.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: There are additional security parameters that can be included in the authorization request to enhance security.
evidence.answer: Optional security parameters (scope, state, code_challenge for PKCE) can be included in the authorization request.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Failure to do so will result in disabling of the application.
evidence.answer: Non-compliance with the API Terms or OAuth Application Requirements results in the app being disabled.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The application and the web address (DNS name) must not include "YNAB" or "You Need A Budget" unless preceded by the word "for".
evidence.answer: The app name and DNS name cannot include YNAB or You Need A Budget unless preceded by the word "for".

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: that an application is sponsored, endorsed, or supported by YNAB.
evidence.answer: The app may not create a false impression that YNAB sponsors, endorses or supports it.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: We are not affiliated, associated, or in any way officially connected with YNAB or any of its subsidiaries or affiliates.
evidence.answer: The site must carry a footer disclaimer saying the app is not affiliated with YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: To identify that your app integrates with YNAB, you may use this linked image and refer to “for YNAB” in the name of your application.
evidence.answer: Apps may use the 'for YNAB' name and a linked image to show they integrate with YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Any graphics or artwork may not be modifications to our official branding and must be distinguishable from YNAB itself and/or from YNAB’s graphics or artwork.
evidence.answer: Graphics must not modify YNAB's official branding and must be distinguishable from YNAB's graphics.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You may not use the YNAB API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.
evidence.answer: Apps may not use the YNAB API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your application may not be directed or for children under 13.
evidence.answer: The app may not be directed at or for children under 13, and the minimum age for a YNAB user is 13.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You are NEVER ALLOWED to directly request, handle or store credentials associated with users’ financial accounts.
evidence.answer: Developers are never allowed to directly request, handle or store credentials for users' financial accounts, other than an OAuth access token from a financial institution.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: This process takes 2-4 weeks.
evidence.answer: YNAB's own docs state that removing Restricted Mode after a review request takes 2-4 weeks. This is the official stated timeline, not a developer-reported experience.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: the application will be limited to obtaining 25 access tokens for users other than the OAuth application owner.
evidence.answer: A newly created YNAB OAuth app starts in Restricted Mode, capped at 25 access tokens for users other than the owner, until a review removes the cap. This is a documented blocker before outside users can connect.
